issue_context.body:

The sense integration does not seem to be able to expose `sensor.energy_production` and `sensor.energy_usage` in the new Energy dashboard in core-2021.8.0

The 2 sensors returns the instant energy consumption and production coming from the sense monitor.

Troubleshooting seems to indicate a bug in the integration on how statistics are exposed https://www.home-assistant.io/more-info/statistics/

Also seems like the devices attached to Sense cannot be added to the new Energy Dashboard because they output in Watts, not KWH.

Maybe we can get the dashboard to calculate that and allow the devices from Sense.

> Also seems like the devices attached to Sense cannot be added to the new Energy Dashboard because they output in Watts, not KWH.

Sense devices show instantaneous power usage (watts or kilowatts), would have to update the integration to include the historical usage (watt-hours or kilowatt hours)
Really looking forward to using my Sense for this if the integration is updated. Thank you all for the hard work!

@kbickar 

The 2 sensors that I noticed being present today are `energy_production` and energy_usage` they represents respectively the instantaneous solar production and home usage of the house. 

Now looking at the energy dashboard configuration HA seems to require 3 values:
1) energy production: this can probably be associated with the sensor mentioned above as we get that value in time.
2) grid consumption: this I think is not available today and I think should be the difference of max(0,energy_usage-energy_production)
3) return to grid: same as above but this time max(0, energy_production-energy_usage)

I was trying to dig a bit in the documentation and is unclear to me if the energy dashboard wants a long term metered entities so the integration needs to keep track of the time interval to convert it to power and expose the last_reset or if HA takes care of it.

I was able to use `sensor.daily_production` and `sensor.daily_usage` as inputs to two template sensors for "grid consumption" and "return to grid" (max of 0 and the relevant difference). This worked fine(*) during the day.

But there's another issue: for me the daily reset occurred at 12:02:32 am, not 12:00:00, despite what the "last_reset" property claims. So the day started out with large negative daily production and usage. I'm not sure if this is due to polling schedule, daily reset schedule at Sense, or something else.

(*) -- worked fine until Sense had an unrelated outage yesterday due to an expired SSL cert
@crkochan  Will this 0.9.2 version automatically add a grid return sensor without needing to make a custom one?

The library version adds additional property decorators to the underlying data object returned from the Sense API, and allows for integrations to query for the data from the object as well. It's the first step in making that data available in Home Assistant.

The step after that is to update the existing integration to add new sensors. This is the PR  that is currently under review.

If merged, the PR would add grid sensors without any user input. Instead of having two sensors (usage and production) for each time scale (daily, weekly, monthly, and yearly), there would be seven. 

The core devs are rightly concerned about introducing additional sensors that users might not be interested in without the means to easily disable them.
I just got a Sense. Same issue. I would assume this also affects Wiser as that is just a rebranding of Sense for Square D to resell

review_comments:
Sense should move to using `SensorEntityDescription`, it will make it more clear what sensors are being defined. [Example](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/54846/files#diff-cf5109edebb2f7b936709887b718df72730a593027d49aef6c399c033439f8bbR39)

Another benefit is that you will be able to implement `entity_registry_enabled_default=False` to avoid having all these new entities show up.

Hello. Long time user, first time contributor.

I agree that `SensorEntityDescription`s are a great idea, I'm just wondering if that work should be part of this PR. 

The more I look into the concept, and look at how it's been done in other integrations, it seems like it implementing it will increase the scope of the PR. Plus, as I said, I'm new at this and it's going to take longer than it would a more seasoned contributor to do this work.

What % does this represent? 

I think that we should consider not adding all these entities by default. Please disable by deafult a couple of non-relevant ones by setting `self._attr_entity_registry_enabled_default = False`

I have[ a PR open on the docs repo](https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant.io/pull/18983) that explains the editions.

In this case, these two sensors are reported as percentage values from the API for...
*  Net production as a percentage value ( energy produced / energy consumed * 100 )
* Solar powered percentage values, which is supposed to be a representation of the amount of power produced from solar that went to power the household and not exported to the grid ( 100 * (usage - from_grid) / usage )

From Sense community posts, the solar powered % number is easily the least interesting, and I will admit that it was just something I added because it was there. 

I'm working toward having `OptionsFlowHandlers` that would allow for switching on or off entire sensor classes, like having active sensors, but turning off per-device sensors, as well as letting users choose which trend sensors they want to be enabled.
 
That said, it's easier to type all that then it is to implement it, and I'm at the the `Hello World` stage of adding the flows themselves. It's going to take more time for me to get them fully implemented, figure out how to translate those choices into the actually reconfiguration of the integration, and then figure out how to update the tests.

Let's disable these by default.

```suggestion
            self._attr_native_unit_of_measurement = PERCENTAGE
            self._attr_entity_registry_enabled_default = False
```
Home Assistant already has options to disable entities, we shouldn't duplicate those features with an options flow.
